thread:
sre-bot: INCIDENT STARTED 2623456789 - GPU OOMs on inference-prod in us-west-2 :rotating_light:

matt_h: seeing a surge of CUDA OOMs across 3 nodes. containers are crashing even though headroom shows ~600MB free.

jin_server: confirmed - looking at node gpu-13, nvidia-smi shows high allocation but free memory reported in headroom metrics.

liz_ops: cc @oncall-maya - customers hitting 503s, tailing logs now.

oncall-maya: oncall ack, joining. quick question: is this the same pattern as last week's reserve evaporation?

matt_h: feels different. last week was reserve drift, this looks like immediate allocation fail when a multi-request batch hits.

jin_server: digging into allocator logs. saw this pattern: repeated small allocations filling reserved blocks, leaving many tiny free fragments. allocator tries to allocate a big contiguous KV cache chunk and fails.

liz_ops: paste of klog snippet:
````
[2026-02-12T12:01:11Z] cuda: alloc 1.2GiB failed despite headroom 0.9GiB, reserved_slabs: 4 sizes, free_fragments: 312, largest_free: 64MiB
[2026-02-12T12:01:11Z] caller=serving/runtime/alloc.cpp:453 try_alloc -> OOM
````

oncall-maya: that largest_free 64MiB is the giveaway - request needed ~1.2GiB contiguous. fragmentation.

matt_h: any paging/prefetch activity before the failure?

jin_server: yes. I see a background prefetch job firing for a large LLM shard right before the OOM bursts. It tramples the reserved pool with many small grabs.

liz_ops: metrics: KV cache hit ratio dropped, prefetch throughput spiked. customers on model-x get errors.

oncall-maya: initial mitigation idea: disable prefetch on the affected shard, force immediate reclaim of tiny fragments, and roll nodes out gradually.

matt_h: agree. also add a quick hotfix to prefer slab merging on reclaim path. but that needs a tiny runtime patch — could take 30-40m.

jin_server: temp mitigation: set serving.runtime.prefetch.enabled=false for model-x via config rollout. Apply to one node as canary.

liz_ops: running command: `rdwctl config set serving.runtime.prefetch.enabled model-x false --env=prod --region=us-west-2 --selector=gpu-13`

oncall-maya: applied to gpu-13 canary. monitoring logs.

matt_h: meanwhile, restart failing containers on other nodes with a smaller max_batch size to avoid big contiguous allocations. `kubectl rollout restart deploy/inference-runtime -n prod --env=us-west-2` but update env var MAX_BATCH=64 on the deployment.

jin_server: done on node pool small-batch. crash rates dropping on those nodes.

liz_ops: customer impact note: approx 12% of production requests for model-x served with 503s between 12:00-12:25 UTC; mitigated to 2% after canary.

oncall-maya: excellent. can we confirm no memory leak? need to ensure reserve accounting not steadily losing blocks.

jin_server: allocation counters: reserve_count stable, but fragmentation metric up. no leak. it's fragmentation + prefetch race.

matt_h: root cause hypothesis: prefetch loop issues + slab allocator fragmentation prevents satisfying large contiguous allocations even though aggregate headroom > request. allocator does not attempt aggressive coalescing until low-memory fail path triggers, which in some code paths is short-circuited.

liz_ops: found a stack trace from a crashed container: `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation at serving/kernel/kv_cache.cpp:112` and then `SIGABRT` on oom handler.

oncall-maya: action items: 1) keep prefetch disabled for model-x in region until patch, 2) deploy slab coalescing patch to runtime repo (matt), 3) increase headroom threshold alert to catch fragmentation earlier (liz), 4) run fragmentation defrag job on idle nodes (jin).

matt_h: I'll open a PR with a small change to force coalesce on reserve reclaim + unit test. tagging `infra-alloc` reviewers. ETA 45m for PR, 1h for rollout to prod after signoff.

jin_server: scheduling defrag cron: `rdwctl maintenance defrag-gpu --selector=region=us-west-2 --concurrency=2` will compact free fragments by draining small batches, runs with minimal customer impact. starting now on one node.

liz_ops: increased alert: `ALERT GPU_FRAGMENTATION_HIGH` threshold lowered from 80%->65% and added `largest_free` dimension.

oncall-maya: do we need customer comms? status page updated?

liz_ops: posting status: "Partial disruption for model-x in us-west-2; mitigations in progress, reduced errors after config changes." Will update with root cause once patch merges.

matt_h: note for postmortem: discuss making allocator more fragmentation-aware, re-evaluate prefetch window sizing, and consider constrained contiguous allocation path (attempt smaller split allocations or fallback to spill-to-disk).

jin_server: monitoring looks stable on the canary. starting staged rollout of prefetch disable across nodes + applying MAX_BATCH change.

oncall-maya: keeping oncall for next 2 hours. if errors creep above 5% revert and escalate.

liz_ops: final metrics snapshot at 12:45 UTC: error-rate model-x us-west-2 = 1.8% (down from 12%), avg latency +0.2s from baseline due to smaller batches, GPU util steady.

matt_h: PR opened: `github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/5123` with coalesce-on-reclaim, tests passing. requesting emergency merge.

oncall-maya: approved merge and rollout to canary.

jin_server: canary patch rolled to one node. no regressions. scheduling full rollout in 10m.

liz_ops: status updated on status.redwood.ai. customers notified of recovery.

oncall-maya: incident class: Sev-2. assigning postmortem owners: matt_h (root cause), jin_server (mitigation + defrag), liz_ops (customer comms + alerts).

matt_h: thanks team. will write up timeline and submit postmortem doc. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED 2623456850 - main mitigations applied, monitoring watch continue for 2h.

end of thread
